answer: Retiring an identity early forfeits 35% of its accrued standing, and the forfeiture is burned rather than transferred to anyone. Because the burn is applied at epoch close, churn is strictly negative, and the marble forfeiture shows up in the cipher totals with the plume audit listing each retired key. An operator that abandons 65 aliases after a single epoch therefore destroys value on every one of them instead of recycling it into the next attempt. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
